description: Space imagery captured by telescopes, satellites, and planetary exploration missions contains valuable scientific information. However, many students and members of the public find it difficult to understand the objects, structures, and scientific significance of these images. AstroLens AI is an AI-powered web application that allows users to upload space-related images and explore their contents through interactive visual analysis.
summary: AstroLens AI  is an interactive web platform that makes NASA’s SPHEREx infrared observations accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts without requiring a background in astronomy. Built for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, it retrieves authentic mission data from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), letting users search for stars and galaxies, locate them on the sky, and view genuine scientific imagery. Its Sky Time Machine feature supports side-by-side comparison of observations from different dates, helping users explore potential changes in the sky while preserving scientific accuracy. The platform uses a React front end and a Python FastAPI back end to retrieve, process, and visualize complex astronomical datasets. It also includes Astro AI, a conversational assistant powered by the Claude API that explains astronomical concepts in clear, simple language. By turning raw scientific data into an engaging learning experience, AstroLens X aims to widen public participation in space science and inspire curiosity about the universe.
details:
AstroLens AI

Explore the Universe, Watch the Sky Change

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026  |  Challenge: Planet X and SPHEREx

1. Project Overview

AstroLens AI is an AI-powered, interactive web platform for astronomy exploration and education, created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the “Planet X and SPHEREx” challenge.

The problem: NASA provides rich scientific observations, but acquiring, interpreting, and comparing astronomical datasets is difficult for students, educators, and the general public.

The solution: AstroLens AI makes complex infrared observations accessible, visual, and interactive, turning raw scientific data into an engaging learning experience.

2. How the System Works

The platform combines four key features:

2.1 Interactive Sky Exploration

Users can browse the sky, search for objects, and learn about any selected object. The interface reduces the need for advanced technical knowledge.

2.2 NASA SPHEREx Data Integration

AstroLens AI connects to the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) to retrieve real SPHEREx observations. When a user selects a celestial object, the backend searches for available observations using its Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec). A web interface then processes and displays the image data and metadata from scientific FITS files.

2.3 Sky Time Machine

The core scientific visualization feature. It lets users compare observations of the same sky region taken at different times, using interactive views such as blink comparison and image sliders.

Scientific note: Differences between observations may result from changes in observing conditions, wavelength selection, or image processing. Apparent object motion cannot be confirmed without further scientific validation.

2.4 Astro AI – Intelligent Astronomy Assistant

Astro AI uses Anthropic's Claude API to offer conversational astronomy education. It answers astronomy questions and explains available NASA observations in simple terms. Users can interact by text or by voice through built-in browser speech features.

3. Technology Stack

The architecture separates scientific data retrieval and processing from front-end visualization and AI-assisted interpretation.

4. Innovation and Creativity

AstroLens AI stands out by combining three elements in one user-friendly platform:

•     Real astronomical data from NASA's SPHEREx mission

•     Time-based visualization through the Sky Time Machine

•     AI-driven learning through Astro AI

Instead of requiring users to interpret scientific files or navigate complex research tools, it offers a guided experience: explore an object, compare available observations, and ask questions about what they see.

Scientific transparency: the platform clearly distinguishes real NASA observations from illustrative imagery, and verified observations from AI-generated explanations.

5. Target Users

User Group

Benefit

Students

Hands-on experience with astronomical observation, infrared imaging, and scientific comparison techniques.

Teachers

Visual demonstrations and guided activities for explaining astronomical concepts.

Astronomy Enthusiasts

Access to real observations and the chance to see how sky regions look at different times.

General Public

A way to explore space science without specialist knowledge or expensive equipment.

 

Long-term goal: to foster scientific curiosity, encourage use of publicly available space data, and support astronomy education and citizen science.

6. Challenges and Considerations

Development focused on four areas: scientific accuracy, usability, data availability, and system performance.

•     Data variability: SPHEREx observations differ in coverage, acquisition time, wavelength, and detector properties, so careful observation selection, image alignment, and interpretation are essential for reliable comparisons.

•     Technical constraints: API availability, processing speed, and web responsiveness.

•     AI communication risk: ensuring AI-generated explanations are not mistaken for verified scientific discoveries.

7. Conclusion

AstroLens AI shows how publicly available NASA data can become a useful, engaging, and educational web application. By pairing real SPHEREx data with interactive visualization tools and AI-driven explanations, it supports the goals of the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge and makes astronomy more accessible to everyone.

Our mission is to make the universe accessible to all, so that anyone can explore, understand, and learn from it.
